source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed building fire-safety checks

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
3. Specify the location and unique identifier of the building (e.g., address, name, or ID number) in the report.
4. Record the date and time of the inspection, along with the inspector’s name and credentials.
5. List all areas and components that were due for inspection, such as fire alarms, sprinkler systems, fire extinguishers, emergency exits, and signage.
6. For each inspected component, describe any issues found in detail - malfunctioning equipment, missing parts, expired components, or noncompliance with standards should be documented clearly.
7. Take photographs or videos as visual documentation of deficiencies or failures.
8. Include the specific standards or codes that were not met (such as local fire safety codes, NFPA standards, or other regulations) and cite them in the report.
9. Document any corrective actions that were recommended during the inspection.
10. Note any follow-up visits or re-inspection dates scheduled to verify
